questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A nice place to live and interesting courses at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The university in the Netherlands was very good at informing me about anything I needed to know, and there were also Whatsapp groups where you could ask any questions you had.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None as I just did everything myself, but they offered to meet you at the train station. A week or two later, there were also meetings at the university where they informed you about practical things like finding a doctor, using the university's intranet etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and found housing quite easily via Idealis, but many other students had trouble finding housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The town is small so it is quick to get to campus even though you live in a different part of the town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was cheap, but quite gross as the building was old and not particularly well maintained, and the people in my corridor did not prioritize cleaning. But otherwise, it was okay.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the courses you would like to take in the course catalogue, and then you choose them in Osiris, and you get a message/mail saying whether you have been accepted or not. Pretty similar to how it works at ku.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask questions in the Whatsapp group, and they also told a little bit about it in an email. You could probably also ask at the student service desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted to take, but I also did not apply to any courses with a limited number of seats where students from particular programmes had priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to sign up for courses with a limited number of seats, make sure you sign up early, and also just keep the deadlines in mind in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were good, although there was some overlap with other courses I have already taken.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I primarily took masters courses, but it was easy enough to keep up. I think the level is quite similar to ku. Some of the courses were meant for multiple different study programmes, which meant that they sometimes spent time explaining things that would be quite basic to some people to make sure that everyone understood what was going on. The practicals in the lab and the tutorials where we used Excel or different softwares were very good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures and tutorials were similar. The lab practicals were also similar, although some of them were more "free" as you just got a research problem/question and then had to plan the experiments yourself (with help/assistance from a teacher). Generally, we had more classes that I am used to (around 5 hours every day), but then we had less reading/preparation to do.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Life history of aquatic organisms, Microbial ecology, Molecular aspects of bio-interactions, Seed science and technology, and Wildlife ecology and conservation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses as they were all interesting, although Microbial ecology had quite a lot of overlap with the course Almen mikrobiologi at ku, and Life history of aquatic organisms also used a lot of time to explain concepts that most biology students already know (like natural selection).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I got an unfurnished room, so I had to buy furniture, curtains, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Conventional food was quite cheap, but some organic groceries were expensive. I also only had to buy one book in total while being there, so it was nice not having to spend much money on that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different types of sport at the university sports centre, the different student associations also hosted parties every week, and there were also some other events for students besides that from time to time like story telling evenings, talks, dinners, and farm visits.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join classes or teams at the sports centre (membership is extremely cheap). I also took an intensive one-week beginners Dutch class shortly after I arrived which was fun as you learned a little bit about the language and also got to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit some of the different cities/towns in the Netherlands as it is quick to get around with the train, and also see some of the nature around Wageningen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, it is very similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Same as in Denmark.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Easy to talk with, helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Wageningen is a pretty small town, so not much happens there besides student activities, but it is easy/quick to get to other cities with more things to do. 
2: Start looking for housing early as it can be very difficult, in my opinion using Idealis is best. But also do not worry if you only find something shortly before your arrival as that is the case for many people. You can get priority on Idealis' website a month or so before your arrival, and after I got that, I quickly found a room.
3: Do not worry too much about the exams as it is easy enough to pass.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The train company NS has a weekend offer where you get unlimited travel during the weekends for only around 31 euros pr month.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to study at a different university in a different environment, and also meeting people from different cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was always worrying about the exams, but I ended up doing fine after all.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
